title: Fish stock dynamics: the Schaefer surplus-production model and its prior growth rates

sources.citation: Froese, R., Demirel, N., Coro, G., Kleisner, K. M. and Winker, H. (2017). Estimating fisheries reference points from catch and resilience. Fish and Fisheries 18(3):506-526, doi:10.1111/faf.12190. Author manuscript, NOAA Institutional Repository (repository.library.noaa.gov/view/noaa/63055): Equations 1-2 (lines 139-150), MSY = r k / 4 (symbol list), Table 2.

items.description: Prior range of a fish stock's maximum intrinsic rate of population increase r, by its FishBase resilience class
items.note: Table 2, 'Prior ranges for parameter r, based on classification of resilience in FishBase (Froese and Pauly 2015)'. These are priors for fitting a stock, not a stock's measured r; the model takes the middle of the range.

items.description: Share of unexploited biomass k below which the Schaefer model's surplus production declines linearly (depensation)
items.note: Equation 2: below 0.25 k the surplus r(1 - B/k)B is multiplied by 4 B/k, 'a linear decline of recruitment below half of the biomass that is capable of producing MSY'.
